angle: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (ML systems + spacecraft physics) of the hybrid compute-sail + pod verdict

files.film_locality.py/.json: film decode with weight-stationary expert and per-sequence KV locality, no striping (fill levels optimised)
files.film_striped.py/.json: same plus the best striping the film can do (expert tensor-parallel, KV striping, dense under-fill) with mesh byte-hops charged; 60 model/scenario rows vs the GPU island of inference.py
files.large_batch.py/.json: batch concurrency 2k-32k sequences, TPOT 20 and 100 ms
files.checks.py/.json: spreading FV check, SRAM area/leakage, pod memory capacity, best-credible pod mass, hybrid mass vs pod fraction, 2D tensor-parallel and layer-local MoE cost on the mesh, SEU, shadowing, swarm scale

one_line: The direction survives: mostly film, a small concentrated fraction. The film still wins on mass per watt, by about 3-9x rather than "10x". Many supporting claims are wrong or unproven. Frontier models do not fit in 3-10 m patches. The evidence's film-inference numbers ignore memory locality. SRAM wafer-scale pods cannot hold training state. Tensor parallelism is not the reason pods are needed. SRAM leakage at 85 C is under-budgeted. The design omits storage, CPU/DRAM sandboxes, volatility, and the differential radiation pressure between film and pods.
confirmed: Film lateral spreading: 0.15 W chiplet at 2.54 cm pitch, 30 um c-Si + 13 um Mg: die-to-mean dT 9.1-10.3 K (1.5 mm2 die, k_Si 148-120), 6.5-7.4 K (6 mm2 die). The 10 K claim holds. The c-Si absorber carries ~2/3 of the heat; Mg alone would give ~27 K.
Film areal density 0.172 kg/m2 sums correctly from its items (c-Si 0.070, glass 0.050+0.0125, Mg 0.0225, structure 0.012, grid 0.004). Film 0.89 g/W (0.47-1.98) is plausible.
Concentrated A at 7.2 g/W is internally consistent and lighter than SpaceX AI1 (~13 g/W at 75 kW/t). The heat-transport tax is structural, so a better pod narrows the gap but does not close it.
MoE expert all-to-all at 31-47 % of energy reproduces for patch-wide routing over 68-137 hops (1.4e-4 B/FLOP x 3.7 pJ/B-hop). With layer-local expert placement it falls to ~8-12 %.
Cross-island bandwidth for DiLoCo/SparseLoCo-class sync is small (training.json), and Earth I/O is energetically negligible.

errors.claim: Film runs SRAM-resident dataflow inference efficiently. inference.json shows the film 9-160x better than HBM GPUs in tokens/s per kg.
errors.problem: inference.py sets each layer stage to b*FLOP/(n_chips*F*U), i.e. every chip in a layer region shares every token at no cost. Weight-stationary SRAM cannot do that: a routed expert runs only on the chips holding it, and attention runs only where that sequence's KV sits. Recomputed with locality and no striping, film utilisation is 1-5 % and the per-kg advantage 1-8x. Striping fixes this but costs mesh bandwidth. Expert tensor-parallel over 8-64 chips, KV striped over 16-2048 chips and dense chips under-filled 4-128x use 20-29 % of chip power on the mesh, i.e. the whole 30 % IO budget.
errors.correct_value: Frontier MoE (0.67-10T), film/HBM-pod tokens/s per kg at mid masses. Low-to-medium concurrency (64-2048 sequences): 6-90x with overlapped stages, 3-30x without. Batch concurrency (8k-32k sequences), the regime of synthetic data and RL rollouts: 1.8-6x overlapped, 0.8-2x non-overlapped, 0.2-1.7x at pessimistic masses. Film J/token is 0.1-0.7x the GPU's at low concurrency and 1.3-9x at high concurrency. With the best-credible pod (3.9 g/W) instead of 7.2, divide all ratios by ~1.9. Film utilisation 1-44 %.

errors.claim: Frontier models served from 3-10 m patches.
errors.problem: Weights plus KV for 4T-10T models at 16 MB per 0.15 W chiplet and 2.5 cm pitch do not fit. The evidence's own inference.json gives 17-33 m. The interconnect study recommended patches of 1 m2 or less.
errors.correct_value: 4T-10T: 17-30 m sides at 2k concurrency or less, 30-100 m at 8k-32k. 0.67-1T models: 8-18 m. Only models of about 0.5T or less, at modest concurrency, fit in 10 m. Sides grow 1.4-2x if leakage limits a 0.15 W chiplet to 4-8 MB.

errors.claim: Pods are wafer-scale SRAM modules for tightly coupled training islands.
errors.problem: Wafer SRAM holds ~1.8 MB/W (Cerebras WSE-3: 44 GB at ~25 kW), against 115 MB/W for HBM (Rubin) and 107 MB/W for the film. A 1e26-1e28-FLOP MoE replica holds 115-1154 TB of state (16 B/param x1.25).
errors.correct_value: At ~1.8 MB/W, SRAM-wafer pods need 64-641 MW per replica; HBM pods need 1.2-12 MW and film 1.3-13.5 MW. Training pods must be HBM/DRAM and shielded. Google Suncatcher saw HBM irregularities at ~2 krad, so ~5 g/cm2 of shielding is required.

errors.claim: The film cannot do tensor or expert parallelism, so pods are needed for TP/EP training islands. interconnect_final puts Megatron TP on a film group at 53-96 % of energy.
errors.problem: That figure uses a 1D Megatron layout. A 2D (SUMMA-style) weight-stationary layout on the mesh costs ~2.5/sqrt(params per chip) byte-hops per FLOP, independent of d.
errors.correct_value: 2D TP: 1.4-3.5 % of energy for inference, 3.6-13 % for training (16-40 B/param). Layer-local expert all-to-all in 1e27-1e29 MoE training: 15-31 % (10-22 m layer regions, 3-6 us). The film can host dense training and, at a cost, MoE training. Pods are justified mainly by DRAM-capacity CPU work, storage, switching and MoE-heavy or hedge training.

errors.claim: ~10x more FLOP/s per kg of Mercury (0.9 vs 7.2 g/W).
errors.problem: (a) This is peak FLOP/s; film decode utilisation is 1-44 % against ~50 % assumed for GPUs. (b) It applies to pure film: the recommended hybrid with 3-10 % pods is only 4.7-6.6x. (c) The pod is not the best concentrated design. A pod with a 353 K radiator at 1.3 kg/m2, short two-phase SO2 loops and a 0.8 kg/kW module reaches 3.9 g/W (2.2-6.6).
errors.correct_value: Peak FLOP/s per kg, film over best-credible pod: ~4.8x (2.9-8.9x), including the pod's +12-20 % J/FLOP at Tj 105-120 C. Hybrid at 15 % pods: 1.85 g/W, 3.9x over pure thermal_mass pods (2.9x over best pods). Each 1 % of power moved into pods adds ~7.2 % to total mass.

errors.claim: SRAM-only chiplets at 0.15 W and Tj 85 C, with SRAM leakage plus control at ~15 % of chip power (workloads/common.py).
errors.problem: The film is memory-heavy: 16 MB per 0.15 W is 107 MB/W, ~60x Cerebras and ~100x Groq. The 3-nm ISSCC low-leakage figure (27.5 uW/Mb at 25 C) times the project's own 25-85 C factor of 4-24 gives 15-89 mW. With 100 pA/cell active leakage it gives 40-240 mW.
errors.correct_value: SRAM leakage is 10-59 % of chip power (retention basis) or 27-160 % (100 pA/cell). The film then holds 2-4x less SRAM per chip (wider patches) or loses 1.3-2x compute per W. Mitigations: non-volatile MRAM/RRAM for read-mostly weights (no standby power, SEU-immune, survives brownouts), or Tj 60-70 C at ~1.0-1.07 AU, which conflicts with staying inside Earth's orbit at higher coverage.

errors.claim: Manufacturing: the same die area per MW as modules, 47 x 300 mm wafers per MW (0.75-1.5 mm2 dies).
errors.problem: A 16 MB SRAM chiplet as used by the workload model is ~6 mm2 (5.0 mm2 SRAM at 35.5 Mb/mm2 with 25 % periphery, plus logic). That is ~40 mm2/W of leading-edge logic silicon, against ~5 mm2/W for an HBM GPU (and the HBM's DRAM uses a different, denser process).
errors.correct_value: ~640 leading-edge 300 mm wafers per MW, 13x the claim. Mass is negligible, but fab throughput, not Mercury mass, is the likely build-rate limit, and it favours HBM pods per W.

errors.claim: DiLoCo-class low-communication methods between islands, for 1e27-1e29 FLOP runs.
errors.problem: Largest public low-communication pretraining: Covenant-72B (SparseLoCo, 72B params, ~1.1T tokens), about 4.7e23 FLOP by 6ND (my estimate; the paper gives no FLOP total). INTELLECT-1 is ~6e22 FLOP. DiLoCo scaling laws go to ~10B params, and quality degrades with replica count (+1.1 % loss at M=8, 2.4B). Frontier runs are ~3e26-1e27 FLOP. At the Earth-safe swarm (3.2e36 FLOP/s) a 1e29 run is 3e-8 s of swarm time, and 1 % of the swarm for a year is 1e42 FLOP.
errors.correct_value: The claim is unproven by 3-6 orders of magnitude. Swarm-scale training would mean millions to billions of islands, for which no method exists. Training throughput per model is capped by algorithms, not by the pod fraction.

errors.problem: Epoch AI puts OpenAI compute at ~5:2 R&D to inference in 2024 ($5B vs $2B) and roughly even in 2025. It holds only if RL rollouts (inference-like, but counted as R&D) are included.
errors.correct_value: Not established. Plausible as a trend. Do not make the architecture hinge on it; the film's ability to train (error 4) reduces the dependence.

errors.claim: One energy-per-FLOP basis across the evidence.
errors.problem: thermal_mass uses 7.8e-14 J/FLOP (system, 85 C, under-clocked). workloads uses 0.15 pJ / 0.55 = 2.7e-13 J/FLOP for film chips and 1.43e-13 for the Rubin all-in.
errors.correct_value: Absolute swarm FLOP/s differ 3.5x depending on the source file. Pick one basis for the visualization.

errors.problem: Frontier-2028 4T has 405B of non-routed (every-token) params but 120B active (3.8x inconsistent); Kimi-K2 class 1.42x. This penalises the film model, which touches the dense bytes, but not the GPU model, which uses 2*Na.
errors.correct_value: Corrected in film_striped.py by capping dense bytes at Na minus active routed.

errors.claim: Thin c-Si film: AM0 20 % at 30 um; 20 um glass cover made from Mercury materials.
errors.problem: 20 % AM0 at 30 um is about 5-10 % optimistic. A soda-lime-type glass (~9 ppm/K) on Si (2.6 ppm/K) leaves ~100 MPa tension in a 20 um cover after processing, so it must be a SiO2-rich Mg-aluminosilicate or fused silica (0.5-4 ppm/K).
errors.correct_value: Design detail. It does not change the mass.

missing_considerations: Differential radiation pressure: film beta ~0.005 vs pods ~0.0005 gives da ~3e-5 m/s2 at 0.92 AU, ~1 km/s per year (110 km of drift per day from rest; 70 m/s along-track for co-radial circular orbits). Film and pods cannot hold km-scale formations without ~2.5 %/yr EP propellant or matching sails (~+0.5 g/W on pods). Sail-to-pod links are long-range handover links, so only pod-only clusters can be Suncatcher-class.

Shadowing and volatility: the umbra is ~99x the occulter size at 0.92 AU, so a 100 m pod or radiator shades ~10 km downstream. Any brownout wipes SRAM weights and KV. Formation rules must keep pods off film sun-lines, and the film needs a backing store and a reload path.

Storage and CPU/DRAM: agentic RL needs environments, tool sandboxes (1-16 GB DRAM each; 4 GB = 312 film chiplets), datasets, checkpoints and weight stores. None is film-hostable, and DRAM/NAND need shielding. Estimate 3-15 % of power in shielded CPU/DRAM/flash pods, absent from the verdict.

Soft errors: an unshielded 16 MB chip sees ~0.1-13 upsets/day quiet and ~1e3-1e5 in large SEPs (low-energy proton direct ionisation through ~1-12 mg/cm2). SECDED (+12.5 % bits) with 1-100 Hz scrubbing keeps uncorrectables at or below 5e-4 per chip-day except in extreme events. Logic silent data corruption needs ABFT/residue checks (~2-5 %); pause during big SEPs.

Fault tolerance: at 0.13 %/yr (0.007-1.2 %) a 30 m frontier patch (1.4M chips) loses ~5 chips/day (0.3-46), plus ~0.1 % dead at bonding. Each loss stalls the layer pipeline until remap, so it needs spare chips, detour routing and a weight backing store. Film training replicas (1e7-1e8 chips) lose a chip every 0.5-80 min. Recovery from DiLoCo sibling replicas, not checkpoints, is needed.
Pipeline occupancy: decode needs 61-128 or more concurrent sequences (one per layer stage) to fill the layer pipeline. Single-agent long-context streams use ~1/L of a patch.
Location: Earth is 200-1200 s away, so the film's strongest advantage (low-batch, latency-bound decode) only benefits in-swarm agents. For batch work the advantage shrinks to ~1-6x per kg.

RL across heterogeneous hardware: rollouts on film chiplets and training in pods worsen the inference/training numerical mismatch, requiring importance-sampling corrections. A 10 TB policy every ~10 min is 133 Gbps sustained per frontier replica, i.e. one Starlink-class terminal per patch plus delta compression.
Attitude: a 1 % reflectivity asymmetry on a 1-km film gives ~11 N.m of torque. About 0.5 % of the area as vanes handles it. Minor.

recommendation.summary: Keep a hybrid with the film as the majority, but re-scope it: ~80-90 % of power on compute sails and ~10-20 % in concentrated pods (baseline 15 %). Pods should be shielded HBM/DRAM/flash modules, not wafer-scale SRAM. Their job is CPU/DRAM agent and RL environments, storage, weight and checkpoint stores, optical switching and gateways, and MoE-heavy or hedge training islands. The film serves frontier inference in 15-40 m patches (30-100 m at batch concurrency), smaller models in 3-10 m patches, and dense or 2D-TP training replicas joined by DiLoCo-class sync. Keep pod power as low as demand allows: each 1 % moved into pods costs ~7 % of total mass.

split.pods_breakdown: 5-10 % shielded CPU+DRAM/flash (sandboxes, RL envs, storage, weight stores, gateways/switches 0.7-2.9 %) + 5-10 % HBM training/capacity islands
split.why: Physics favours the film by ~3-9x in mass per watt, and by 6-90x (low concurrency) or ~1-6x (batch) in useful inference per kg. 2D TP and layer-local EP make film training feasible at 4-31 % comm overhead. What the film cannot host is DRAM-capacity CPU work, non-volatile storage, global shuffles and switching. Those set the pod floor (~5-10 %), plus a training hedge.

key_numbers.FLOPs_per_kg_film_over_pod: ~4.8x (2.9-8.9x) peak; useful inference per kg 6-90x at low concurrency, 1.8-6x at batch concurrency (0.8-2x non-overlapped)
key_numbers.chiplet: 0.15 W at 2.5 cm, dT 7-10 K confirmed. Memory: 4-8 MB SRAM for KV/activations plus non-volatile MRAM/RRAM weights, or Tj 60-70 C if SRAM-only.
key_numbers.mesh_IO_budget: 20-30 % of chip power for striped layouts
key_numbers.placement: film ~0.92 AU (sheet 348 K), pods ~0.86-0.9 AU; pod clusters co-orbit with each other, not with film (beta mismatch)
key_numbers.links: Starlink-class 0.1-0.4 Tbps handover links between sails and pods (one per frontier patch); Suncatcher-class formations only among pods; DiLoCo/SparseLoCo between islands (unproven above ~5e23 FLOP)

spreading.note: dT = die centre minus mean sheet temperature; Si absorber carries ~2/3 of the heat; Mg-only would give ~27 K

pod_capacity.note: Cerebras-class wafer SRAM ~44 GB per 23-27 kW = 1.6-1.9 MB/W; a 0.3-1 MW SRAM pod holds 0.5-1.9 TB.

tensor_parallel_2D.contrast: interconnect_final: Megatron 1D TP on a 16 kW film group costs 53-96 %

seu.mitigation: SECDED (+12.5 % bits) + scrub 1-100 Hz (~0.01-1 % chip power) + ABFT/residue checks on matmuls (~2-5 %); pause on large SEPs

shadowing.note: a 100 m pod/radiator casts a ~10 km umbra; penumbral dimming browns out film cells -> volatile SRAM loses weights/KV
